summary: Los Padres lookout on La Cumbre Peak: 1923 glass house, current experimental cab dated 1945 or 1946, NHLR-registered 2010, now closed to the public and beside a day-use area.

facts.design: Experimental cab with sloped glass and relatively high walls; the only one of its type built, per the Register

access.note: Forest Service says the old fire lookout tower is closed to the public; the site is day use only, reached past a locked gate

visit.trail_note: About a quarter-mile hike past a locked gate to the picnic area on top; the tower itself is closed to the public

events.note: Seasonal glass house on the summit completed in summer 1923 by the Forest Service

May 1938 newspaper notice said the lookout station would open the following Friday
Current experimental cab built in 1945 per News-Press and Peakbagging; the Register description and Wikipedia give 1946

resolved_conflicts.explanation: News-Press and Peakbagging give 1945 for the current cab, and the Register's built field also reads 1945. The Register description and Wikipedia say 1946. The story gives 1945 from the News-Press and Peakbagging and notes the 1946 dates from the Register and Wikipedia.

The Register says the new structure replaced a cabin on a 10 foot open timber tower, so that height belongs to the cabin it replaced; Peakbagging describes the current cab on a 20 foot K-brace tower. The two figures may not describe the same structure, so no height_m is recorded.

Wikipedia and Forest Lookouts describe a seasonal glass house completed in 1923. The Register photo caption describes an original cabin from the 1920s. No source read says the 1923 glass house and the cabin are the same structure.

notes_for_editor: No correction to the brief record: the 1945 built year and the 2010 NHLR registration hold up, though the Register description says 1946. The FFLA list shows status 'RF Hazard' with no explanation; the Forest Service calls the tower closed to the public. Sources describe a 1923 glass house and a 1945/46 cab but do not say whether the cab replaced the glass house or the 1920s cabin in the Register photo caption. Staffing end date and closure date not found; a later Forest Service or FFLA page might give them.
